invariants: The broker never returns a Kick token or client secret to the desktop client.
Authorization request state and PKCE verifier are generated, validated, and destroyed by the broker.
A broker session is bound to application, Kick user, channel, and desktop session slot.
The broker-session credential never appears in a URL or WebSocket subprotocol; WSS uses a single-use short-lived ticket.
Action operation IDs are allowlisted by the frozen Kick contract; arbitrary upstream URLs are rejected.
Kick OAuth fields, channel stream keys, and RTMP URLs are stripped before any response leaves the relay.
Raw webhook bodies are verified before JSON parsing and are not persisted after dispatch.
Disconnect and clear-data invalidate local state; revoke also deletes relay token state when reachable.
